    • \n

Shop Overhead
\n

Shop overhead worksheet

\n
Build the shop’s monthly fixed-cost pool and spread it across expected billed labor hours. That produces shop overhead / billed hr, which feeds each technician’s loaded cost under Staff. Technician wages are entered per tech - not here.
\n
\n Full walkthrough:\n \n ARKademy → Shop overhead and loaded labor cost\n \n
\n
\n
\n \n \n \n \n
\n \n Setup walkthrough - start here\n \n \n
\n
\n

Payroll is split on purpose - there is no single “payroll” box for everything.

\n
    \n
  • Technician wages - Settings → Staff → each tech → Loaded cost calculator (base pay + burden % + shop overhead / hr).
    • \n
  • Advisor, front desk, owner (non-billing) - Fixed Costs tab → Office and advisor payroll (monthly total).
    • \n
  • Break-even on Margin Health - uses this worksheet’s fixed-cost monthly total once saved (shown under Owner Targets). Technician pay is already counted there as labor cost.
    • \n
\n
\n
    \n
  1. Fixed Costs - rent, utilities, insurance, software, equipment, office/advisor payroll, other. Exclude technician straight wages.
    2. \n
  2. Payment Processing - estimated card volume, processor %, optional merchant financing.
    3. \n
  3. Billing Capacity - active technicians, workdays, hours, utilization → monthly billable hours.
    4. \n
  4. Review Shop overhead / billed hr at the top → Save shop overhead.
    5. \n
  5. Settings → Staff - for each technician: base pay, burden %, click Use calculated loaded cost, save.
    6. \n
\n

Example: $8,700/mo overhead ÷ 299 billable hr ≈ $29.08/hr shop allocation. A tech at $30/hr base + 28% burden + $29.08 overhead ≈ $67/hr loaded cost on billed hours.

\n
\n
\n \n
\n
\n

We find the problem before we sell the repair.

\n

Warning light that keeps coming back? Strange noise nobody can pin down? Car running differently? Been given a big repair estimate and want a second opinion?

A repair shop built around doing it right

\n

Shop is a repair shop built around a simple idea: diagnose the vehicle first, explain what we found, and let the customer make an informed decision.

\n

We're not trying to move cars through as fast as possible. Every vehicle that comes through our shop belongs to somebody who depends on it.

\n

Every job is personal.

\n
\n
\n
\n \n
\n
\n

We test before we replace.

\n

A warning light, a noise, or a low reading is a clue. It is not yet the repair.

\n

Before we recommend replacing parts, we test the vehicle against how that system is supposed to work. That can mean scan data, electrical testing, fuel trims, a pressure or vacuum test, and a mechanical inspection. The recommendation comes from what those tests show.

\n

After the repair, the same concern is checked again. The job is finished when the evidence says the problem is gone, not when the part is on the car.
